subject: Clarify: MSA + Order Form — IP title & training/feedback license
messages:
From: Aditi Rao <aditi.rao@meridianhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@meridianhealth.com>, Meridian Legal <legal@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form — IP title and training/feedback license

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — Meridian is excited to move forward. Our legal team reviewed the MSA + Order Form and flagged the IP and "training/feedback" clauses. The key asks from our side:

- We need express ownership of derivative output that becomes part of our patient-facing application.
- We want an explicit option to opt-out of model training using our data.
- We need clarity on whether feedback (bug reports, prompts) can be used by Redwood for product improvements.

I'm attaching a marked-up Order Form (attachment: Meridian_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx). Can your legal folks confirm whether Redwood can make the requested carveouts and, if not, propose alternative wording?

Goal: align on redlines by the end of the week so Procurement can issue the PO.

Thanks —
Aditi Rao
Director, Vendor Management
Meridian Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Rao <aditi.rao@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP title and training/feedback license

Hi Aditi — thanks for the redline and the clear summary. Looping in Ben (account lead) and Laura (legal) to respond with our position.

Quick note from product/sales perspective:
- Output ownership carveouts are something we consider case-by-case depending on downstream productization.
- Training opt-out is typically allowed via an explicit checkbox on the Order Form (we can supply language); there may be pricing implications.
- Feedback as "product improvements" is standard, but we can narrow the license to non-attributable, aggregated improvements for regulated customers.

Laura — can you review Meridian's marked Order Form and share a short list of changes we can accept vs. those that need escalated approval? Aditi — we'll aim to return a counter-redline within 24 hours.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Rao <aditi.rao@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP title and training/feedback license

Aditi — thanks for sending the Order Form redline. I reviewed Meridian_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx and outlined our position below (high-level):

1) Output/derivative ownership
- Meridian request: customer ownership of all derivative output used in their product.
- Redwood position: we grant customers a perpetual, non-exclusive license to use outputs generated by the service per the Order Form. We cannot assign title to outputs universally because some outputs include model-proprietary components and upstream third-party licensed weights.
- Proposed compromise: explicit customer license to "use, reproduce, distribute and create derivative works of outputs for internal productization and end-user facing features", with a carveout that excludes assigning title to Redwood pre-trained model components.

2) Training/data use opt-out
- Meridian request: absolute prohibition on using customer data in any training or model improvements.
- Redwood position: we will offer a per-account training opt-out. We need this in the Order Form as a checkbox and it will trigger a pricing/operational flag.
- Action: I attached a short-form clause (attachment: RWI_MSA_marked_redlines.pdf) and a recommended Order Form checkbox.

3) Feedback license
- Meridian request: prohibit Redwood from using any customer feedback for product improvements.
- Redwood position: we can accept a limited, anonymized feedback license tailored to regulated customers: use for aggregated improvements only, no individual prompt/response retention beyond 30 days for improvement pipelines unless explicit consent is given.

Next steps:
- I've prepared a clean marked MSA with the compromise language and a proposed Order Form checkbox. Please review and send any redlines back.
- Ben — please confirm if sales are comfortable with the pricing delta for training opt-out and I will include that in the counter-offer.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@meridianhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditi Rao <aditi.rao@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP title and training/feedback license

Laura — appreciate the detailed breakdown. A few follow-ups from Meridian Legal:

- The carveout language around "pre-trained model components" is a bit vague. Can you add an explicit definition (e.g., "Redwood Model IP" includes model architecture, weights, pre-training corpora) so we can be sure the customer's generated outputs are not inadvertently limited?
- On the training opt-out: Meridian needs the opt-out to apply to fine-tuning and large-scale training pipelines. If only allowed for small-scale monitoring, it's not sufficient.
- For Feedback: Meridian requests that any prompt examples used for improvements be stripped of PHI and tied to an explicit, documented approval workflow. Aggregation alone is insufficient for our compliance team.

Attached is our second redline (attachment: Meridian_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx) with inline suggestions. If Redwood can draft language that addresses the explicit definitions and a compliance workflow for feedback, we can move to sign-off quickly.

--
Samir Patel
Deputy General Counsel
Meridian Health
